draft_notes.diagnosis:
The failure is in counterexample train pair 2 (index 1). d4=2 is a 180-degree rotation; colour 0 is the box colour and 5 is the background. The visible boxes (y0,x0,y1,x1) are A(0,4,7,8), B(1,15,6,18), C(2,20,5,24), D(8,17,15,27), E(10,2,13,10), F(15,2,17,10), G(21,1,28,11) and H(21,15,28,18).

The candidates whose pipe path is clear, by gap length, are: B-C 1, E-F 1, C-D 2, A-E 2, F-G 3, G-H 3, A-B 6 (horizontal) and E-D 6 (horizontal).

Kruskal accepts the first six edges. That leaves two components, {B,C,D} and {A,E,F,G,H}. The last two edges, A-B and E-D, both connect those two components. They have the same distance (wall-to-wall 7, in both the original and the visible frame) and the same orientation, so the same cdir. The constructor sorts by (dist, cdir, i, j), so the winner is decided only by the generator's internal box indices, which come from the BFS insertion order. That order is a hidden latent. Here the label picked E-D. The failed factory broke the tie by visible coordinates and picked A-B.

No visible rule can recover this choice. Both trees are minimum spanning trees of the visible candidate graph. The prior factory's PREF constant, the d4-based horizontal-first preference, copies a second hidden tie-break (cdir) and cannot resolve same-axis ties anyway.

I also checked the canonical fixtures by hand. In all four (train 1-3 and test), no equal-weight candidate would close a cycle at the point it is considered, so each fixture's MST is unique and its label is consistent with the rule.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: Random scenes require a unique MST of line-clear pipes, with bounded sampling. Equal weights are allowed when they do not create alternative minimum trees. Pipes may enclose other boxes if their two drawn lines are clear. Explicit historical calls remain unchanged. Every dataset episode still requires independent label verification.
